refnamediv.refpurpose: Generate and verify file manifests of directory trees

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-manifest generates file manifests of directory trees, and verifies directory trees against such manifests. Four manifest formats are supported:

listitem.para: A plain list of file names, one per line. Directories are suffixed with a slash.
The format generated by sha256sum1, i.e. a hash and a file name per line. Only regular files are listed. This is the format systemd-sysupdate8 consumes as SHA256SUMS file.
The BSD mtree format, listing inode type, access mode, ownership, size, hash, symlink target and device numbers of each file. This format is supported for generation only.

A UAPI.16 file manifest, i.e. a JSON-SEQ stream with one object per file. This is the format systemd-sysupdate8 consumes as Uapi16Manifest file, and the same format systemd-dissect1 generates with --uapi16. This is the default.

refsect1.para: Manifests are generated and verified in a streaming fashion, i.e. one file at a time, and never loaded into memory as a whole, so that very large trees can be processed.

listitem.para: Generates a manifest of the specified directory tree, and writes it to standard output. If no directory is specified, the current working directory is used.

Verifies the specified directory tree against the specified manifest file. If no directory is specified, the current working directory is used. If no manifest file is specified (or if - is specified), the manifest is read from standard input. If --format= is not specified, the format is derived from the file name of the manifest if possible, and otherwise defaults to uapi16.

Every entry of the manifest is checked against the tree: the file must exist, have the listed inode type and, as far as the manifest carries this information and the --field= setting asks for it, the listed size, hash, access mode, ownership, modification time, symlink target and device numbers. All mismatches are reported, and the command fails if there was at least one. The mtree format is not supported for verification.

Note that the check only goes one way: every file listed in the manifest must exist in the tree as described, but the tree may contain additional files that the manifest does not list. These are not reported, and do not cause verification to fail. Hence a successful verification shows that the tree contains everything the manifest describes, but not that it contains nothing else.

Selects the manifest format. Takes one of list, sha256sums, mtree, uapi16, see above. Defaults to uapi16 for make. For verify defaults to the format derived from the file name of the manifest, and uapi16 if that is not possible.

Selects the per-file fields to include in the manifest when generating, and to check when verifying. Takes a comma separated list of mode, uid, gid, size, hash, symlink, device, hardlink, mtime, user-xattr. The special values all, default and none may be used to select all, the default set or no fields. Items may be prefixed with + or - to add or remove fields from the current set instead of replacing it. The option may be specified multiple times. Defaults to all fields except mtime and user-xattr. Note that the inode type is always included, if the format can express it. Not all formats support all fields: the list format carries no fields at all, sha256sums only the hash, and only uapi16 supports hardlink and user-xattr. The latter covers the extended attributes in the user. namespace of all inodes except symlinks. If enabled, it is recorded for every such inode, including those with no such attributes, so that a verifier can tell missing attributes apart from unrecorded ones.

Selects the hash algorithm to use for the hash field of the mtree format. Takes one of sha256 or sha512. With sha512 a sha512sum= keyword is listed instead of sha256sum=. The other formats only support sha256. Defaults to sha256.

When generating a manifest with make, do not fail if some inodes had to be skipped or some of their metadata had to be omitted, because they could not be read (for example due to missing privileges) or are not representable in the selected format. Instead, log a warning and return success. The top-level inode must be covered by the manifest in any case, but its metadata may be incomplete.

refsect1.title: Exit status
refsect1.para: On success, 0 is returned, a non-zero failure code otherwise. In particular, verify returns non-zero if the directory tree does not match the manifest, and make returns non-zero if an inode had to be skipped or some of its requested metadata had to be omitted, because it could not be read (for example due to missing privileges) or is not representable in the selected format, unless --graceful is specified. In the latter cases the manifest is still generated, but is not written to the output file if one is specified. Inodes other than regular files skipped in sha256sums format are not considered a failure, since this format does not list them by design.

example.title: Generate a UAPI.16 manifest of a directory tree and verify it
example.programlisting: $ systemd-manifest make /srv/tree > Uapi16Manifest $ systemd-manifest verify /srv/tree Uapi16Manifest

example.title: Generate a SHA256SUMS file of the current directory, without ownership or mode information
Only verify file contents, ignoring ownership and access modes
